A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ReMoMask research work. All 13 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original motion-generation and retrieval results, component ablations, qualitative examples, and a user study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative experiments, ablations, and user study, alongside revised qualitative illustrations.

M1.justification: The BMM retriever, SSTA mechanism, 2D RVQ-VAE, masked/residual transformers, and RAG-CFG are unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the training and inference descriptions match.

E1.justification: Both versions use HumanML3D and KIT-ML for the same generation and retrieval tasks. The supplementary user study and qualitative motion scenarios retain their coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3. Figure 6 still compares ReMoMask with MoGenTS, TMR, and ReMoDiffuse; the user study still compares against MoMask, ReMoDiffuse, and ground truth.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, and training settings match. Both user-study descriptions specify 20 prompts, over 50 participants, anonymized models, and randomized presentation. Figure 6's revised examples do not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: The existing qualitative comparison in Figure 6 uses revised baseline examples, changing the visual evidence for motion realism and text alignment. The component and momentum-queue ablations in Tables 4–5 remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point estimates and user-preference percentages without adding repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and the user-study percentages in Figures 3–4 are unchanged. Figure 6 replaces some qualitative outputs, including MoGenTS's walking/rest example and ReMoDiffuse's balancing example, and exchanges TMR's examples between the clumsy- and slow-walking prompt columns. These revisions do not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Equations 1–18 retain the same mathematical definitions, objectives, and operations. No assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and state-of-the-art performance claims. Revised illustrations do not alter their stated scope.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including retrieval weaknesses, deployment cost, limited long-motion validation, abstract-text difficulties, and missing physical verification. No explanation accompanies the substituted Figure 6 examples.

D1.justification: Architecture specifications, hyperparameters, hardware, training duration, and code/project URLs remain identical. The revision supplies no additional implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior motion-generation and retrieval methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: Figure labels receive small wording and punctuation edits, including changing three Figure 6 prompts from 'a person' to 'a man.' The main prose, supplementary narratives, and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 5–6 are enlarged and rebuilt with sharper individual motion panels and typeset labels; Figure 6 also gains row separators. Existing citation and project links become clickable. Tables and the remaining figures retain their presentation apart from small typographic differences.

improvement.justification: The larger, sharper Figures 5–6 make qualitative examples easier to inspect, providing a limited presentation improvement. Scientific descriptions and quantitative support remain unchanged. The baseline-panel substitutions are unexplained, and Figure 6's caption still incorrectly describes three prompts and reverses the displayed row/column roles.
